# North Dakota Public Service Commission cases on generation (2026-10-29)

Cases filed 2022 or later, plus the hand-checked list. The case page and each document in the case's documents folder are stable public links and can be cited. Copies of documents read are in scopes/us-nd/work/psc/ and are not committed.

## Sources

- North Dakota PSC case search: form search by filing date from 2022-01-01 (split into windows until complete), by 13 entity names and 8 description words, plus 23 hand-checked cases; 2140 cases, 415 generation related (https://apps.psc.nd.gov/cases/pscasesearch)
- North Dakota PSC case documents folders: key documents of each gas or generation case downloaded and read (https://www.psc.nd.gov/webdocs/case/)
- North Dakota PSC siting page: siting spreadsheet read, 80 lines kept (https://www.psc.nd.gov/jurisdictions/siting)

  - Application, Electric; filed 2013-04-26, closed 2021-08-31; 224 docket entries; case page https://apps.psc.nd.gov/cases/pscasedetail?getId=13&getId2=194; documents https://www.psc.nd.gov/webdocs/case/13-0194/

  - Megawatts: INTRODUCTION Northern States Power Company, doing business as Xcel Energy, respectfully submits to the North Dakota Public Service Commission this Application for an Advance Determination of Prudence(ADP) pursuant to North Dakota Centur}^ Code § 49-0516, for its proposal to add three 215 MW natural-gas-fired, simple cycle, combustion turbine (CT) generators to its system. | Our analysis, which included significant stakeholder input, identified a capacity deficit of approximately 150 MW that grows to approximately 500 MW in 2019. | On November 21, 2012, the MPUC issued an order establishing a competitive resource acquisition process to determine the resource(s) to meet Xcel Energy’s identified need of 150-500 MW in the 2017-2019 time period. | The first 215 MW combustion turbine would be placed in service in 2017 at the Company’s existing Black Dog plant in Burnsville.
  - Equipment: The model of F class combustion turbines now commercially available has fast start capability, which allows it to reach 150 MW in 10 minutes from a cold start, operate in a range of at least 50 to 100 percent load while meeting emission limits, and achieve faster ramp rates over the load range. | Combustion Turbine Operation and Maintenance The scope and frequency of maintenance work on the combustion turbine(s) will be in accordance with power industry standards and equipment manufacturer recommendations. | The operation and maintenance costs are based on Company experience with similar facilities, as well as industry and manufacturer information. | One of the main tools we used to develop the Company’s proposal and compare it with other types of resources was the Strategist resource planning model.
  - In service: From 2013 through 2020, the average rate of growth in our peak demand forecast is 1.0 percent. | The average growth rate from 2013 to 2020 is 0.7 percent. | The Company based its intermediate facility estimate on the cost of a generic new green field combined cycle power plant project. 34 Public Document Trade Secret Data Excised Strategist simulated the total system cost over the 2013-2050 timeframe. | Table 8 System Cost Comparison of Peaking and Intermediate Alternatives I Total PVRR Incremental Over Peaking 2013- 2050 ($ Millions) Peaking Units: 3 CTs @ 209 MW Intermediate Unit: 1 CC @ 684 MW Units $81,302 $81,519 + $217 The addition of peaking resources tits well with the existing generation in our fleet.
  - Retirements: From 2013 through 2020, the average rate of growth in our peak demand forecast is 1.0 percent. | The average growth rate from 2013 to 2020 is 0.7 percent. | The Company based its intermediate facility estimate on the cost of a generic new green field combined cycle power plant project. 34 Public Document Trade Secret Data Excised Strategist simulated the total system cost over the 2013-2050 timeframe. | Table 8 System Cost Comparison of Peaking and Intermediate Alternatives I Total PVRR Incremental Over Peaking 2013- 2050 ($ Millions) Peaking Units: 3 CTs @ 209 MW Intermediate Unit: 1 CC @ 684 MW Units $81,302 $81,519 + $217 The addition of peaking resources tits well with the existing generation in our fleet.
  - Location: The second and third CTs would be constructed at a new plant site to be located in the Red River Valley near Hankinson, North Dakota (Red River Valley Units 1 and 2) for servdce beginning in 2018 and 2019. | The second 215 MW combustion turbine and associated natural gas, transmission, and interconnection facilities would be placed in service in 2018 at a new site in the Red River Valley, near Hankinson, North Dakota. | Xcel Energy serves approximately 90,000 customers in North Dakota, with the majority of those located in the greater Red River Valley, including the communities of Fargo and Grand Forks. | This site is approximately 70 miles from our Fargo load center, near the juncture of the Otter Tail Power 230 kV transmission system and Alliance natural gas pipeline, thereby providing strong economic justification.

  - Siting Application, Electric; filed 2017-07-17; 159 docket entries; case page https://apps.psc.nd.gov/cases/pscasedetail?getId=17&getId2=284; documents https://www.psc.nd.gov/webdocs/case/17-0284/
  - Technology: combined-cycle
  - Megawatts: NEER is the largest generator of wind-powered electricity in North America, with over 12,400 MW of capacity in 19 states and Canada as of year-end 2015. | In North Dakota specifically, NEER, through its affiliates, owns and/or operates approximately 1,250 MW of wind generation. | AECOM 1-4 July 2017 Foxtail Wind Energy Center 1.3 Certificate of Site Compatibility Project Summary 1 Foxtail Wind evaluated wind resources in North Dakota for siting a 150 MW wind generation facility. | The impact assumptions are shown on Figure 1-4. 1 NEER has been working on the development of a wind farm in Dickey County for several years and previously permitted a 175 MW wind farm through Rough Rider Wind I, LLC (Rough Rider).
  - Equipment: Equipment Procurement, Manufacture, and Delivery: | NSP/Xcel will procure the turbine/tower equipment directly from a manufacturer. | The distances are based on the Hybrid Vestas V-116 turbine, which has a larger rotor diameter than the Vestas V-110 turbine model, and has a total turbine height (from the bottom of the turbine tower to the top of the blade when vertical) of 453 feet. | There are other turbines that are feasible choices for the Project area that are available from various manufacturers and Foxtail Wind wishes to reserve the right to select alternative turbines representative of the Vestas V-116 and V-110 class of wind turbines.
  - In service: NSP/Xcel proposes to continue transitioning from coal to renewables and natural gas (including 35 percent renewable energy from wind and solar by 2030) in its Upper Midwest 2016-2030 Resource Plan (Xcel Energy 2016). | Additionally, according to the Comprehensive State Energy Policy report for 2010-2025 prepared by the EmPower ND Commission, one of the state’s energy goals is to increase installed wind energy capacity to 5,000 MW by 2020 (EmPower ND 2010). | According to the MISO Transmission Expansion Plan for 2016, the MISO region needs to add between 11,400 and 79,900 MW to maintain planning reliability targets through 2030. | Comprehensive State Energy Policy 2010-2025.
  - Retirements: NSP/Xcel proposes to continue transitioning from coal to renewables and natural gas (including 35 percent renewable energy from wind and solar by 2030) in its Upper Midwest 2016-2030 Resource Plan (Xcel Energy 2016). | Additionally, according to the Comprehensive State Energy Policy report for 2010-2025 prepared by the EmPower ND Commission, one of the state’s energy goals is to increase installed wind energy capacity to 5,000 MW by 2020 (EmPower ND 2010). | According to the MISO Transmission Expansion Plan for 2016, the MISO region needs to add between 11,400 and 79,900 MW to maintain planning reliability targets through 2030. | Comprehensive State Energy Policy 2010-2025.
